articleTitle: Yield optimization of high frequency superconducting digital circuits with genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Even simple superconducting logic gates can contain tens of inductors, resistors and Josephson junctions. In order to increase the yield and reliability of such suboptimal circuits to acceptable levels, it is often needed to adjust all the element values. The search space is therefore very large, and genetic algorithms have been used with remarkable success to optimize such gates.

articleTitle: A posteriori error estimation results for the fem analysis of a waveguide filter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The use of an explicit, residual-based, a posteriori error indicator for directing a single-level p-refinement of the finite element method analysis of a waveguide filter is investigated. Hierarchical, curl-conforming elements of various orders are employed. It is shown that substantial improvements upon uniform element polynomial order discretizations can be obtained in terms of accuracy versus number of degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Intrinsic motivation of students in project based learning
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Educational thinking in higher education has undergone a rapid change. The ability to remember facts loses importance whereas the capability to solve problems becomes more and more the main focus of teaching. At the Technikum Wien Project Based Learning (PBL) was introduced in various subjects of our IT course. The basic approach of PBL originated from the University of Maastricht in the Netherlands where it is reported to be highly successful [1-4]. The specific problem the authors tried to solve, deals with the motivation of students. The main motivation of students is -of course to achieve good test results and only the lesser focus lies on the specific contents of the subject. The authors tried to develop a method, which allows the students to focus their intrinsic motivation onto the study project itself and not onto the extrinsic motivation, namely test results.

articleTitle: Evaluation and effective management of nontechnical losses in power networks
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Market-driven economies and deregulated electricity industry environment have stimulated the minimization of technical and non-technical losses (NTL) even though they do not constitute major operational or quality of supply problems. Their impact is economic and utilities often passed down the costs to consumers. NTL need to be addressed to determine the overall performance of power networks, as these losses are expected to be more dominant at the sub-transmission (132kV-33kV) and reticulation (22kV and 11kV) levels of the electricity supply industry value chain. In some national grid operations, NTL are estimated to account for up to 30% in revenue losses to electric utilities, and overhead expenditure in added maintenance costs. This paper discusses a method for NTL evaluation and an effective management approach to loss minimization and revenue collection.

articleTitle: A Web-based interactive database and corba tutorial
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: With Web-based open and distance learning students can study and train when and where they want - even from home. Based on a database, CORBA middleware and Web frontend, we have implemented an interactive database and CORBA tutorial to allow for efficient, interactive student training. Our system also supports the testing of the student's application in a distributed environment together with a real-life database. Students can concentrate on their main tasks and need not waste time and effort learning to use complicated tools and configuring environments. Consequently, they grow familiar with complex e-commerce technologies in a convenient way.

articleTitle: Increasing value from projects by leveraging limited capacity through the application of the theory of constraints
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper introduces the concepts of the Theory of Constraints as developed by dr. E. M. Goldratt and others. When applied to a portfolio of projects, the value that an organisation realises from successful delivery can be maximised. A new value metric is introduced that effectively accounts for the flow of money in different time periods. An approach to portfolio management that strives for maximising organisation performance, given limited organisational capacity, is also introduced. Critical Chain project scheduling and synchronising projects around the schedule of a heavily loaded (drum) resource are used as the methodology of finite capacity management that enables leveraging value with scarce resources. A new set of buffers is introduced to enable the integration of portfolio management and Critical Chain scheduling.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of multidimensional trellis coded modulation and convolutionally coded MC-DS-CDMA in a rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we investigate the performance of multidimensional (Multi-D) trellis coded modulation (TCM) and low rate convolutionally coded multicarrier (MC) code division multiple access (CDMA) schemes in a Rayleigh fading channel. In both systems, the output of the encoder modulates multiple band-limited DS-CDMA signals, which are then transmitted simultaneously at different carrier frequencies. Although low rate convolutional codes (CC) perform better than multi-D TCM, TCM systems are more bandwidth efficient for the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and number of carriers.

articleTitle: Detection of broken rotor bars part I - New theory
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Conceptually, a broken rotor bar in a squirrel cage induction motor would imply an open circuit in one of the bars. On the contrary, research [1] has shown that in most, copper cage motors, the contact impedance between bar and core is small, allowing current to continue to flow into the broken bar. This current enters the broken bar, and flows through the core to the adjacent healthy bars, as interbar currents. The paper shows that these interbar currents produce an axial force, and by monitoring the associated frequencies - interbar current and consequently broken rotor bars are detected at an early stage of development such as a high resistance joint (bar-end ring joints) or one broken bar. Experimental measurements in part II of the paper verify the theory presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a prototype computer based rehabilitation device for the lower extremities
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes the design, construction and implementation of a personal computer controller adapted for the use of the lower leg. Strain gauges are attached to the ankle and interfaced to a PC via the games (joystick) port where ankle movement is used to control any number of joystick games and applications, thereby providing a motivational means of exercise and rehabilitation. A flexible diagnostic tool, for assessing the condition and rehabilitation of a patient, was developed. The feasibility of the device was investigated in the laboratory and with clinical experiments and was shown to be a viable tool capable of giving accurate indications of injury and movement limitations.

articleTitle: Instrumentation for the measurement of the thermal conductivity of hydrating concrete
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Knowledge of the thermal conductivity of hydrating concrete facilitates more accurate thermal modeling. This information coupled with thermal management techniques, reduce the risk of crack formation during the curing phase in large concrete structures. In this paper, the thermal conductivity probe method of measuring the thermal conductivity of hydrating concrete is described together with the design considerations necessary for the successful implementation of the technique. The design of a portable instrument capable of performing thermal conductivity measurements in-situ and the algorithms used to automate the measurement process are presented.

articleTitle: A proposed empirical model of the effective earth radius factor for telecommunications use in South Africa
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Available data for the cumulative probability of occurrence of various values of the radio refractive k-factor fot South Africa have been subjected to regression analysis in terms of a proposed equation to describe such a distribution. The results presented have considerable promise in predicting the average cumulative trend of the k-factor in the inland summer rainfall areas. The model is expected to be of value in predicting large values of the k-factor, which may only be exceeded relatively rarely, but which could give rise to long-range interference in radio communication systems.

articleTitle: Common problems in the performance measurement of profit and cost centres
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The interaction of the measurements of cost centres and profit centres, and the resultant effect on an organization's profit is examined by applying the Theory of Constraints thinking processes. Two cases are described based on the measurements that a profit centre should maximize profit and a cost centre should at least recover its costs. These cases illustrate that some outsourcing decisions taken in isolation can lead to a spiral of declining competitiveness; and that the attempts by a cost centre to maximize cost recovery leads to a lower profit for the organization. The thinking process logic shows that these negative effects are caused by the application of wrong measurement criteria.

articleTitle: Maintenance management - A neglected dimension of engineering management
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Engineering management comprises the management of resources as well a number of life-cycle engineering processes, such as development, production and maintenance. A life-cycle approach towards the management of technical assets calls for a balanced approach in which all life-cycle phases are addressed. The management of maintenance is a relatively new academic and knowledge area. Within the engineering management body of knowledge the management maintenance has not yet received the attention that it should get. The focus is still on development of new systems rather than maintenance and support. This paper outlines the role of maintenance in the business enterprise and how the discipline of maintenance management can be enhanced in organisations.

articleTitle: Guest editorial: WCDMA and coding for the fading channel
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The appearance of this Special Edition of the Transactions of the SAIEE coincides with the dawning of a new era in multimedia wireless access. Not only is the third generation (3G) wireless systems in the process of being deployed, but also broadband Personal Communication Systems and Networks (PCS and PCN). In those areas where the 3G roll-out is still being contemplated, interim 2.5G extensions of the existing 2G (GSM and IS95) cellular standards, such as GPRS, EDGE and cdma2000, are already under way. Elsewhere, especially in Europe, Asia (Japan and China) and the USA, 3G cellular standards (UMTS/3GPP and 3GPP2) are already operational in many main centra.

articleTitle: Regular papers section: Identifying and developing the attributes of technology leaders in telecommunications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper examines the attributes of technology leaders in the telecommunications industry. We define the telecommunications technology leader at three levels, the specialist, the integrator and the chief technology officer. Inputs to the description of attributes of these types were obtained from a survey of leaders in the three categories. The attributes are presented in the form of a core problem-solving competency with characteristic deliverables, underpinned by a body of knowledge, and exercised in a complex, changing environment. A four-tier model for the leader's body of knowledge is presented. The paper identifies important inputs to the development of telecommunication technology leaders and the role of postgraduate programmes in particular.

articleTitle: Self-excitation in pwm inverter excited single-phase induction generator
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A single-phase induction generator is being excited and regulated by the means of a controllable charged capacitor connected to a PWM inverter feeding the auxiliary winding. In the absence of an external source the voltage build-up in such a generating scheme depends on self excitation taking place. This paper, therefore, analyzes the conditions for selfexcitation in the generating system. Consequently, the basis for designing for self-excitation is established Three possible configurations of the generating system are investigated for selfexcitation.

articleTitle: Detection of broken rotor bars part II - Experimental verification
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Experimental measurements on three squirrel cage induction motors are presented to verify the theory developed in part I of this paper. The axial vibration and stator current spectra were measured on all three motors. The first is a 55kW motor having large interbar currents, while the remaining motors are two, identical 75kW motors, one with a broken bar (having small interbar currents) and one with a healthy cage. A comparison between the axial vibration and stator current measurements are made, showing that while the stator current technique uses the magnetic disturbance to detect the fault, the axial vibration technique relies directly on the interbar currents present in the motor. As interbar currents are present in the initial stages of the fault, early detection of broken rotor bars can be achieved by monitoring the axial vibration. This correlates with the theory presented in part I of the paper.

articleTitle: A genetic algorithm for impedance matching
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A genetic algorithm is used as the basis for a new impedance matching algorithm. The new algorithm obtains similar results to published techniques in most cases despite not requiring transformers.

articleTitle: Feasibility study and prototype development for the measurement of pressure contours under the human foot
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A cost-effective device for determining pressure contours under a human foot has wide application in medical diagnosis, rehabilitation and sports medicine. This paper details feasibility study and prototype development of such a measurement system. The system scans a grid of quasi-discrete pressure sensors formed by pairs of electrodes and a sheet of Teledeltos paper and provides a numerical output with graphical representation. With a resolution of 6 mm and a speed of 10 frames per second the system provides a low-cost solution to determine pressure contours under a human foot and could provide dynamic pressure measurement of a runner.

articleTitle: Implementing first world technology systems in third world industrial systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Unique challenges face the implementer of novel advanced technology in industries. This is even more so when the industry in question is located in a third world country. This paper reinvestigates this problem from a technology / industry system point of view and presents a new model for understanding these challenges.

articleTitle: Practical considerations for interference suppression cylindrical arrays
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The practical considerations in the design of a cylindrical array for interference suppression, is presented. The influence of the mutual coupling between the antenna elements on the degree of suppression is investigated. The possibility of correcting the element input impedances for certain array configurations is also studied.

articleTitle: Changes in course presentation to accommodate the “Information age” and outcomes based requirements
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The “traditional” lecturing style, of presenting students with information during lectures and examining their ability to grasp and retain this information, no longer meets the outcomes for engineering graduates as required by the Engineering Council of South Africa. As a result of the outcomes based requirement and the easy access to electronic information the style of teaching, in the final Electronics and Measurement Systems courses, has been changed to a “workshop” styled system design with the responsibility left to the students to obtain the content information. Initial findings indicate that, although there was initially extreme resistance by the students at the start of the course, their self-confidence improved with better results for the particular course and the design course that it supports.

articleTitle: Application of extended huygens' principle to scattering discontinuities in waveguide
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A recently proposed extended Huygens' principle for scattering objects in waveguide is reviewed. This technique allows the coupling of a Finite Element discretization with a quasi Method of Moments (MM) surface element approach. Perfectly conducting posts are considered as test cases. Implementational details are discussed and results for the conducting post are presented.

articleTitle: Improved generalized low-density parity-check codes using irregular graphs
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we introduce the construction of new families of error-correcting codes based on irregular low-density parity-check codes (LDPC), which we called generalized irregular low-density (GILD) codes. GILD codes are constructed by replacing each single parity check in LDPC codes with the parity check matrix of a small linear block code called the constituent code. The average weight distribution of GILD codes over all possible interleavers is derived as a function of the component code and the code length N. We also study iterative decoding of GILD codes for communication over an additive while Gaussian noise channel. The high flexibility in selecting the parameters of GILD codes and their better performance make them more attractive than GLD codes and hence suitable for small and large block length forward error correcting schemes.

articleTitle: Voice over internet protocol detail records for the session initiation protocol
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: As the telecommunication industry is moving from a circuit switched network to a packet switched network, features like Voice over IP, Video over IP, Video on Demand, etc. will become more important. Currently two protocols for multimedia on packet switched networks exist. The one is H.323 and the other is the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP). At this stage, it cannot be determined which one will gain dominance over the market.

articleTitle: Power and spectral efficiency performance of a family of WCDMA-modulated constant-envelope root-of-unity filtered complex spreading sequences in non-linear power amplification
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper compares the spectral and power efficiency of a new WCDMA multi-dimensional modulation strategy, employing a class of constant-envelope root-of-unity (CE-RU) filtered complex spreading sequences, with conventional Nyquist filtered QPSK-modulated CDMA employing binary spreading sequences in the presence of non-linear power amplification. The comparison is based on Complementary Cumulative Probability Density Function Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (CCDF-PAPR) measurements, as well as the amount of spectral regrowtb experienced when the power amplifier is driven close to the 1dB saturation point. Simulation as well as hardware results are presented to illustrate the superiority of the new complex-spreaded multi-dimensional WCDMA modulation schemes over conventional 3G methods in terms of spectral and power efficiency in the presence of non-linear power amplification.

articleTitle: Analysis of a PV-battery-inverter single-phase induction generator
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The analysis of a hybrid photovoltaic (PV) and single-phase induction generating scheme suitable for producing both controllable load voltage and frequency is the theme of this paper. This scheme has a potential utility in industrial and commercial applications, and in utility as an embedded generator. A battery connected across an array of (PV) cells is connected to a bi-directional, single-phase PWM inverter feeding the auxiliary winding of the induction generator. It supplies the generator reactive power, with the battery either absorbing excess power provided by the turbine or supplying deficit power to meet the active power demand of the load connected to the main winding. This paper presents the dynamic and steady state models for analyzing this scheme and reports the findings of the experimental and analytical cum computer simulation works undertaken to establish the performance characteristics of the generator. Parametric studies useful for optimal design and operation of the scheme are also discussed.

articleTitle: Industrialisation guidelines methodology
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The industrialisation of any new technical system requires the establishment of the required industrial infrastructure and supplier base for the system. This paper describes a methodology for the determination of industrialisation guidelines for such programmes. The methodology considers three types of considerations. They are 1) Strategic & Operational Requirements, 2) Market Considerations, and 3) Current Industrial Capabilities. These are evaluated and the scores are combined to calculate the recommended industrialisation guidelines. There are four possible outcomes or guidelines that this methodology produces. They are for 1) Local procurement, 2) Overseas procurement, 3) Partnership procurement, or 4) Competitive procurement. Two examples of the application of this methodology are given. These are for the armaments industry and the Pebble Bed Modular Nuclear Reactor project.

articleTitle: Increasing the bandwidth of a microstrip patch antenna with a single parallel resonant circuit
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Results are presented to show that the impedance bandwidth of a microstrip patch antenna can be improved substantially by adding a single parallel LC resonator in the form of an open- and short-circuited stub to the feed structure of the antenna. Computed and measured results are presented, demonstrating a bandwidth improvement of more than 100%.

articleTitle: A Consideration of computer laboratory infrastructure in engineering education
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Computer laboratories used in engineering education are investigated by considering the requirements, constraints and infrastructures involved. Three primary requirements are identified: to provide access and connectivity, to support the teaching and learning process and to provide assessment facilities. The use of fat client and thin-client infrastructures in engineering education is discussed using two computet laboratories at Wits University as a case study.

articleTitle: Regular papers: PWM of a modular inductive storage millisecond pulse-forming network
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Millisecond pulse-forming networks are used to generate an energy pulse of up to several Megajoules in a defined pulse shape and time span. Passive pulse-shaping methods are often used. An alternative is to use switches to commutate energy from a storage medium into the load. The type of storage medium and the power levels used define the switch type. For capacitive storage, one requires a turn-on switch, for inductive storage, a turn-off switch is required, and for battery storage, a turn-on/turn-off switch is generally required. Such a system usually requires a staged energy transfer. In order to shape the pulse, either a final pulse-shaping stage can be included in the system or a modular system can be employed. This paper discusses the use of PWM to approximate the pulse shape as required. This allows the reduction of the number of modules and greater control over the discharge pulse shape. Results using a two-module system are presented and a comparison is made to a four-module system not using PWM.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of the LCDCM blind multiuser detector in frequency selective channels
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper we will see that the linearly constrained differential constant modulus (LCDCM) detector is well suited for blind multiuser detection. A DS-CDMA signal model is presented, which is used as a platform to analyze the LCDCM cost function. The LCDCM cost function is investigated and the fact that it has a global minimum is confirmed. Finally, comparative simulation results in AWGN and multipath fading channels are investigated and discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of tariff on dial-up internet traffic: Modelling the subscriber response as a dynamic system
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper contributes by providing a linear differential equation which captures the response of residential dial-up subscribers to a tariff function. South African data was gathered on residential subscribers who were making use of cheaper off-peak rates for dial-up Internet service outside business hours. Traffic intensity was found to be heavily dependent on the call tariff, with the steepest increase in traffic occurring at the time of rate changeover. It was also unexpectedly found that the traffic intensity dropped off exponentially as subscribers completed their tasks. The subscribers' response to a tariff change was then treated as a dynamic system, with input x(t) being the excitation function, representing the tariff imposed by the single network operator, and an output y(t), to represent the function of the traffic resulting from the imposed tariff. The response to the sudden tariff decrease was thus captured in a linear differential equation. Using the equation, the subscribers' response to a set of interesting tariff scenarios has been predicted. As a result, recommendations for superior tariffing are made.

articleTitle: On the viterbi decoding of linear block codes
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the trellis decoding of binary and non-binary linear block codes using of the Viterbi Algorithm (VA) in a variety of mobile channels. The construction of Bahl-Cocke-Jelinek-Raviv (BCJR) block code trellises is described, as well as the application of a block-wise VA to these trellises as an optimal Maximum-Likelihood (ML) decoder. Both hard and soft decision decoding is considered, as well as the incorporation of Channel State Information (CSD in the calculation of VA branch metrics. An extensive simulation study is presented to validate the VA as an efficient ML block code decoder. Simulation results are presented for hard and soft decision decoded binary Hamming and non-binary Reed-Solomon (RS) block codes under varying Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) and flat fading channel conditions. The Bit Error Rate (BER) performances of reduced and unreduced trellises are also compared. Special attention is given to the influence of CSI on the BER performance of Viterbi decoded linear block codes. Unique contributions made by this paper in the field of linear block coding include: Novel techniques for binary and non-binary block code BCJR trellis expurgation and reduction. BER performance results for VA decoded non-linear RS block codes in flat fading channel conditions employing varying degrees of CSI, and simulation results for the VA decoding of a binary cyclic linear block code employing a reduced trellis structure.

articleTitle: On a new family of complex spreading sequences with zero cross-correlation properties
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: In this paper, a novel family of root-of-unity filtered complex spreading sequences is introduced. The new sequences, called Constant-Envelope Root-of-Unity filtered Zero-Cross-Correlation (CF-RU-ZCC) sequences, are a non-linear derivative of a family of polyphase sequences originally proposed by Suehiro et al. CE-RU-ZCC sequences can be shown to exhibit superior properties compared to the former, with little correspondence with the original Suehiro source sequences, apart from their desirable autocorrelation properties, which are perfectly retained despite the RU-filtering employed. The sequences are shown to be unique in several ways. Firstly, the unique lillering method results in sequences with perfectly constant envelope when modulated onto quadrature carriers, resulting in superior power efficiency compared to Nyquist-filtered sequences The sequences secondly exhibit zero cross-correlation amongst the members of a family, and are therefore of particular interest in multi-user cellular environments, such as wireless CDMA, where thirdly, their use results in a significant reduction in multi-user interference (MUI). The new sequences finally have excellent spectral efficiency, their power spectral distributions (densities) being practically equivalent to Nyquisl-filtered sequences with sharp spectral roll-off. The paper includes results to verily the various claims made, and compares the CE-RU-ZCC sequences to several of the more commonly known spreading sequence families, such as the binary Gold family and the family of so-called generalised chirp-like (GCL) sequences originally proposed by Popović.

articleTitle: Reflection plane placement in numerical inductance calculations using the method of images for thin-film superconducting structures
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Accurate calculation of the inductance of thin film structures in sub-Terahertz superconducting logic circuits is extremely important. For a numerical analysis, both the structure and ground plane need to be sufficiently segmented. The method of images significantly reduces the number of segments required, but the selection of the position of the reflection plane is critical. The influence of the position of the reflection plane on inductance is investigated, and results presented. A study of segmentation and filamentation is also made, and these results are used to calculate the inductance of a complex three-dimensional structure.

articleTitle: How will the new entrant telecommunications operator benefit from being new?
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Following the general worldwide trend of de-regulation and privatisation of the telecommunication market, the South African Government issued an Invitation to Apply for the second Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) licence. The Second National Operator will be issued with a PSTN license to provide competing services. The entry of such a New Entrant Operator (NEO) into the territory currently occupied by a monopoly Incumbent Operator (10) will be built on a sound case for doing the business.

articleTitle: Antenna amplitude distributions for improving wireless power transmission efficiency
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The methods and algorithms of the amplitude distribution synthesis used for increasing the Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) efficiency are discussed. It is shown that WPT efficiency increases not only at the uniform or taper distribution but also when the field intensity is raised at the edges of the radiating apertures. In this case the receiving antenna (rectenna) is illuminated uniformly enough and the level of the near side lobes is essentially decreased. Peculiarities of requirements on the field are described. Some numerical results concerning the optimal field distributions on the antenna and in the rectenna plane are presented.

articleTitle: Preface to special section
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It is our pleasure to present several papers from the High Frequency Techniques and Antennas Session from the IEEE Region 8 AFRICON '02 conference held in George, South Africa from 2-4 October 2002. By its very nature this is a fairly general conference, which addresses many issues in the field of electrical, electronic and computer engineering and which are regarded as being of importance to development in Africa. The fields of interest covered range from Aerospace and Electronic Systems, through Computer Science and Systems to Engineering Management and Power Electronics and Drives, amongst others.

articleTitle: Preface to the engineering management section: Engineering management and competitiveness
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Technology is a major driver of global economic development and because it is an expensive resource, the management thereof has to be a high priority for business managers in order to ensure optimal utilisation. In the last decade. Technology Management, or in the broader sense Engineering Management, attracted considerable attention from practitioners and academics. This is not surprising if we look at the rate of emerging new technologies in almost all industries around the globe. Computing, telecommunications, bioengineering, automotive, and so forth, are only a few of the sectors well known for the rapid changes in technology. It can thus be expected that companies, universities and research institutions will reflect this trend in their own product & process development projects, educational programmes and research activities. Engineering Management is defined as the link between engineering, science and management and uses a typical lifecycle approach as its basis. The management focus thus falls on the optimisation of technology and its related processes like innovation, project management, systems engineering, product development, operations and maintenance management, economic viability studies, and more. These are issues of concern to engineers of all disciplines and from all industries.

articleTitle: Preface to the engineering education section
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Changes in engineering education, both in lecturing styles and curriculum, have been ongoing since the advent of the training of engineers. This is as the result of changing technology and social conditions, both in terms of what is required from the engineer and the abilities of the students entering the programme. Engineering educators have had to adapt their training to provide society with competent and adaptable engineers.

publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The University of Pretoria's new facility - the (“AFC (Computer Aided Education Centre) - has conic into action. The infrastructure is part of the Faculty of Engineering. Built Environment and Information Technology.

abstract: Circuit Breaker Industries (CBI) is a South African company with over half a century of experience in the design and manufacture of a comprehensive range of technically advanced products for electrical protection. These are primarily circuit breaker and earth leakage protection devices for residential and industrial applications as well as a range of metering products. CBI products are used by supply authorities/utilities, mining, industry and in millions of households.

abstract: Vodacom has continued to increase its customer base in the face of generally turbulent market conditions where investors lost confidence in the telecommunications sector. Boasting cellular subscribers of more than 8,6-million across its operations in South Africa. Tanzania, Lesotho and the Democratic Republic of Congo -Vodacom still commands its leading position as Africa's biggest mobile phone operator. Nearly eight million of these customers are based in South Africa. This has necessitated that we continually expand the capacity of our local network infrastructure to accommodate the increasing volumes of subscribers. Vodacom has 5000 base stations reaching 94% of South Africa's population. As the company marks next year its symbolic 10th anniversary of being in operation next year, it is ever more determined to maintain its leading market position and achieve sustainable growth in profits and cash flows. To that end, high performance standards remain our critical focus.
